findings.element: 2026 consensus brackets table — 'KEY VIEW' column
findings.detail: The 'Key View' column text is visibly cut off for every institution row (e.g., Goldman Sachs shows 'fading tariff drag growth, below-c', BCA Research shows 'Two-stage 2026: tech broad selloff HQ as labo oil, tech capex t'). The column container is too narrow and clips the commentary mid-sentence, making it unreadable in a board context.

findings.element: Sector tiles — commentary text blocks
findings.detail: Multiple sector tiles (e.g., Pharmaceuticals/GLP-1, Residential Real Estate, Commercial RE, Auto Manufacturing, Federal Government) contain body commentary that is clipped at the bottom of the tile container, with sentences ending mid-word or mid-phrase. Content is not fully visible.

findings.element: Sector tiles — body commentary text
findings.detail: The body text inside all sector tiles (Passenger Airlines, Hotels, Restaurants, Grocery, E-Commerce, Software & Cloud, Pharma, Residential RE, Commercial RE, Auto Manufacturing, Federal Government, Freight & Logistics) is rendered at an extremely small font size (~7–8px equivalent), making it effectively unreadable at normal viewing distance for a CEO-level audience.

findings.element: Source lines beneath charts and tables
findings.detail: Source attribution lines (e.g., under Exhibit 01, Exhibit 02, the consensus table, and the bottom synthesis section) are rendered at very small font sizes with low contrast against the background, making them difficult to read.

findings.element: Exhibit 02 — grouped bar chart, x-axis labels
findings.detail: The x-axis category labels on the right-hand consensus bar chart (e.g., 'Fed Funds Rate %') appear compressed and partially obscured, with some label text running together or being cut at the chart boundary.

findings.element: 'So what' commentary beneath Exhibit 01 (Quarterly GDP chart)
findings.detail: The 'So what' note reads: 'The Q4 deceleration into +1.4% is the cleanest run-rate signal — 2026 enters with weaker momentum than the full-year +2.2% suggests.' This is only 1 sentence, which is fewer than the minimum 2 sentences required.

findings.element: 'So what' commentary beneath Exhibit 02 (consensus bar chart)
findings.detail: The 'So what' note beneath the right-hand chart is a single sentence ('Consensus is bracketing a soft-landing path with growing tail risk — the dispersion between forecasters is wider than at any point since 2022'). This violates the minimum 2-sentence requirement.

findings.element: 'So what' commentary beneath the 2026 consensus brackets table
findings.detail: The 'So what' note ('Stanford SIEPR sits at the bearish end (~40% recession odds); Goldman is the clearest soft-landing voice. The dispersion is the headline — not the midpoint.') contains only 2 sentences and is borderline acceptable, but the first sentence uses hedging phrasing ('clearest soft-landing voice') that may not meet directness standards.

findings.element: Sector tiles grid — 'Federal Government' and 'Freight & Logistics' tiles
findings.detail: The bottom row of sector tiles (Federal Government, Freight & Logistics) appears to have inconsistent tile heights and spacing compared to the rows above, with the two tiles not filling the full grid width, creating visual imbalance.

findings.element: Sector tiles — internal padding variation
findings.detail: The internal top padding and spacing between the SNP/GDP metric badges and the commentary text block varies noticeably across sector tiles (e.g., E-Commerce tile appears more compressed than Passenger Airlines), inconsistent with uniform panel treatment.

findings.element: Sector panel mini-charts — bar labels and commentary text
findings.detail: The year labels, percentage annotations, and commentary text beneath each sector bar chart are rendered at an extremely small size (estimated 6–7 px). At board-deck zoom levels these are unreadable without magnification.

findings.element: Footer source line at very bottom of page
findings.detail: The full-width footnote/source string at the bottom of the dashboard is rendered at approximately 6 px and is illegible at normal viewing distance, violating minimum legibility standards for a CEO-level document.

findings.element: Multiple sector panel titles (e.g., 'Inv. Banking', 'Pharma/Biotech', 'Chips/Hardware', 'Aerospace/Def.')
findings.detail: Several sector panel titles appear abbreviated or truncated to fit the card width (e.g., 'Inv. Banking' for Investment Banking, 'Aerospace/Def.' for Aerospace/Defense). While some abbreviation is acceptable, the truncation is inconsistent across panels and may confuse a board audience.

findings.element: Bottom summary table commentary block ('Real GDP held 2.0% in 2025 — but the sector mix is tilting toward defensives')
findings.detail: The explanatory headline/commentary for the bottom GDP-by-sector table appears to be embedded as a header row within the table section rather than as a clearly separated 'fc-note' block preceding the chart. Style guide requires commentary to precede the first chart element on each section.

findings.element: Bottom GDP table section vs. sector card grid above
findings.detail: The vertical spacing between the sector card grid and the bottom summary table section appears noticeably larger than the spacing between other major sections on the tab, creating an inconsistent rhythm.

findings.element: GDP Commentary — 2025 Growth & 2026 Outlook text block
findings.detail: The top commentary block contains 4 sentences but includes hedging filler language ('it is a backward-looking figure', 'most exposed', 'if credit conditions do not ease') that softens the analytical stance rather than delivering a direct, assertive insight. Style guide §2 forbids hedging filler and requires direct declarative sentences.

findings.element: Sector card grid — 'Cruise Lines' and 'Travel Agencies' bottom row
findings.detail: The final row of sector cards contains only two cards ('Cruise Lines' and 'Travel Agencies') while all other rows contain six cards, leaving a large blank area to the right. This asymmetric row creates an unfinished appearance in a board-level document.

findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: Unemployment tab
findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: TOP SECTOR metric tile (KPI card row)
findings.detail: The 'Top Sector' KPI tile displays 'Investmen t Banking' with a mid-word line break splitting 'Investment' across two lines, making it appear as two separate words. This is a clear rendering defect visible at board level.

findings.element: EX 4 Sector wage growth bar chart — axis labels (left side)
findings.detail: The sector name labels on the Y-axis of the horizontal bar chart (EX 4) are extremely small and difficult to read at dashboard zoom level, making the chart effectively unreadable for a CEO/board audience.

findings.element: Source footnotes beneath EX 2, EX 3, EX 4, and EX 5 charts
findings.detail: Source attribution text beneath multiple charts is rendered at a very small font size (appears sub-8pt), making it illegible without zooming in. While footnotes are intentionally small, the all-caps dense blocks are below readable threshold for a board deck.

findings.element: EX 3 chart — subtitle/annotation text block below chart
findings.detail: The 'So what' analytical commentary line below EX 3 and the dense source block are rendered at extremely small font sizes, making them unreadable at normal viewing distance in a board presentation context.

findings.element: EX 2 line chart — X-axis date labels
findings.detail: The X-axis date labels (Aug '23 through Nov '26) appear tightly spaced and some labels may overlap or be difficult to distinguish cleanly at the rendered resolution.

findings.element: EX 1 Wage Growth Commentary — fc-note text block
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging language ('essentially zero') and runs as a single very long run-on sentence block that is difficult to parse. Style guide limits commentary to 2–4 sentences; this block appears to be a single dense paragraph that may exceed readable sentence structure norms.

findings.element: EX 3 and EX 4 side-by-side panel row
findings.detail: EX 3 (left panel) and EX 4 (right panel) appear to have unequal vertical heights and bottom padding, with EX 3's source block extending lower than EX 4's boundary, creating visual misalignment between peer panels on the same tab.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 — Annual CPI is still well above the Fed's 2% target after three years
findings.detail: The chart area for Exhibit 4 is completely blank. No bars or data are rendered despite the subtitle indicating a dec-to-dec YoY % U.S. city average series should be present. Only the source line is visible at the bottom.

findings.element: Exhibit 5 — Goods inflation has normalised; services and shelter remain sticky (left panel)
findings.detail: The chart area for Exhibit 5 is completely blank. No grouped bars or data are rendered despite the subtitle indicating a dec-to-dec % change by category comparison should be present.

findings.element: Exhibit 6 — Category-level annual rates show four still above 3% (right panel)
findings.detail: The chart area for Exhibit 6 is completely blank. No data is rendered despite the subtitle indicating a dec-to-dec % change by category sortable table/chart should be present.

findings.element: Exhibit 7 — Trimmed-mean and median CPI track headline — inflation is broad, not concentrated
findings.detail: The chart area for Exhibit 7 is completely blank. No line series are rendered despite a legend showing Headline CPI MoM (ann.), Trimmed-Mean CPI, Median CPI, and Fed 2% Target being present.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — Energy and transport categories are pulling the basket higher (right panel bar chart)
findings.detail: The chart area for Exhibit 3 (right side) appears blank — no bars are rendered for the Sep'25 accelerating, Sep'25 cooling, and Aug'25 category comparison despite the legend being visible.

findings.element: All exhibit subtitles, source lines, and axis labels throughout the tab
findings.detail: At dashboard viewing resolution, subtitle rows (e.g., 'CPI-U ALL URBAN CONSUMERS · MONTHLY TOY READINGS…'), source attributions, and axis tick labels are rendered at extremely small font sizes and are effectively illegible without zooming in, which is unacceptable for a board-level deck.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 'So what' callout — left panel
findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary note for Exhibit 3 (left panel) appears below the chart rather than above it, violating the requirement that fc-note commentary precede the first chart on each panel.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 'So what' callout — right panel
findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary note for Exhibit 3 (right panel) appears below the chart rather than above it, violating the requirement that fc-note commentary precede the first chart.

findings.element: EX 5 & EX 6 bottom panel — axis labels and data labels
findings.detail: The x-axis year labels and bar chart data labels in both the Housing Starts (EX 5) and Affordability Index (EX 6) panels are extremely small and difficult to read at dashboard viewing scale, falling below acceptable legibility thresholds for a board-level document.

findings.element: EX 4 — Mortgage rate gap chart axis labels and data point annotations
findings.detail: The y-axis labels and annotated data point values on the mortgage rate gap vs. Fed funds rate chart are rendered at a very small font size, making them illegible without zooming in. This is unacceptable for a CEO/board audience.

findings.element: Source footnotes — all panels
findings.detail: Source attribution text at the bottom of multiple panels (EX 2, EX 3, EX 4, EX 5, EX 6, EX 7) is rendered at an extremely small font size, making it effectively unreadable in the dashboard view.

findings.element: EX 7 Metro table — 'Market Note' column
findings.detail: Several entries in the 'Market Note' column (e.g., Detroit, MI row: 'Fastest-appreciating major market from low base: UAW effect') appear to be at or near the edge of the column container, risking truncation on narrower viewports or in print.

findings.element: EX 2 — 'So what' commentary block
findings.detail: The 'So what —' commentary for EX 2 appears below the chart rather than above it, preceding the first chart as required. The style guide mandates that fc-note commentary precede the first chart on each panel.

findings.element: EX 3 & EX 4 — 'So what' commentary blocks
findings.detail: The 'So what —' callout text for both EX 3 and EX 4 is positioned below their respective charts rather than above them, violating the rule that commentary must precede the first chart in the panel.

findings.element: EX 6 — Affordability Index bottom sub-panel (Months Supply line)
findings.detail: The bottom sub-panel of EX 6 shows a line chart for Months Supply with a reference line (balanced market at 6.5 mo), but the legend is extremely small and may not clearly distinguish the series from the reference line at board viewing scale.

findings.element: EX 1 Housing Commentary — introductory paragraph
findings.detail: The opening commentary block contains hedging language ('still active') and runs to approximately 4–5 sentences, potentially exceeding the 4-sentence maximum. The phrase 'is a shock–level move' is borderline sensationalist rather than analytical.

findings.element: EX 5 and EX 6 panels vs. EX 3 and EX 4 panels
findings.detail: The vertical spacing between the panel title/subtitle and the chart body appears inconsistent between the upper row (EX 3/EX 4) and the lower row (EX 5/EX 6), with the lower panels appearing more compressed.

findings.element: EX 7 Metro table — Detroit, MI Median Price
findings.detail: Detroit, MI shows a Median Price of '$220K' which is bold/highlighted differently from other rows, but more critically the formatting convention (bold for outlier vs. standard) is not explained in a legend or footnote, creating ambiguity for a board audience.

findings.element: Section 2 — Oil Supply Shock Tracker daily closes chart (axis labels and annotations)
findings.detail: The x-axis date labels and several inline annotations on the daily WTI/Brent line chart are rendered at a very small font size and are difficult to read at dashboard viewing scale, particularly the session-count and date range labels beneath the chart.

findings.element: Full Oil Impact Chain table — node detail rows (body text)
findings.detail: The descriptive body text inside each node row (e.g., 'Describes retail moves within days of a WTI shock…') is rendered at an extremely small size, making it unreadable without zooming in — inappropriate for a CEO/board-level deck.

findings.element: Section 4 — bottom source line and footnote text
findings.detail: The multi-source attribution line at the very bottom of the dashboard is rendered at a font size that is effectively illegible at normal viewing resolution.

findings.element: Section 3 — Sector Impact table source/disclaimer line
findings.detail: The italicised disclaimer text beneath the sector margin table ('Source: Morgan Stanley…') is too small to read without magnification.

findings.element: Section 4 — 'Past shocks averaged ~12 months' table, 'Economic Consequence' column
findings.detail: Several entries in the 'Economic Consequence' column appear to be cut off or wrapped in a way that truncates the trailing text, particularly the Mar 2026 row where the Fed cut timeline note is clipped.

findings.element: Section 4 — Recession Signal History commentary block
findings.detail: The orange-highlighted 'fc-note' commentary paragraph for Section 4 appears to sit between the section header and the charts, which is correct in principle, but the block visually bleeds into the chart area below rather than being clearly separated above the first chart, risking misread as a chart caption rather than a preceding note.

findings.element: Section 4 — Recession Signal History fc-note commentary
findings.detail: The commentary contains hedging language ('causality is debated', 'typically contribute', 'Worth monitoring if') which violates the prohibition on hedging filler. The note also runs to approximately 5 sentences, exceeding the 4-sentence maximum.

findings.element: Section 2 vs. Section 3 panel gap
findings.detail: The vertical gap between the Section 2 and Section 3 panel dividers appears noticeably larger than the gap between Section 1 and Section 2, creating inconsistent inter-section spacing across the tab.
